Did some testing on older systems, RHEL 9 both Qt 5 and Qt 5.

On Qt 5, the ApplicationPaletteChanged signal gets received by windows before the tokens get parsed after a new theme is applied, so there are warnings about unknown tokens like HeaderSection and HeaderSectionHover.

Also on Qt 5, the parsing of Qt6 QFont strings isn't quite right. The weight values are different in the two versions, so Qt 6 uses a map to translate from the old style to the new style. This only really has a visible effect if the MR is hacked so that the QApplication sets its monospace font when the theme updates (I know you will do a real solution later), but it makes the font max weight regardless because the ranges are very different.

On older GNOME systems, there's no switch for Light vs Dark mode, people just selected a dark variant of a theme. That doesn't seem to work with the "System" option here. On current master, it sort of works at startup but not necessarily later.

"HeaderSection and HeaderSectionHover" - that can be expected as the "defaulting" behaviour is not finished yet. The order of receiving the signal is an important info, will investigate that. 

The switch back I will investigate
https://github.com/qt/qtbase/commit/9803ba9b6f74f5ac18220fe145fe1fe4c8f70910 appears to be related to why Qt 5 widgets get an earlier signal.

Each of the three systems handles colour and palette changes differently. It is unbelievable how broken those parts of Qt are. I will take a look if there is a different way to monitor the changes to avoid relying on signals from Qt for Qt5.
The regression on older GNOME systems should be addressed in the next update.
The Qt 5 signal-ordering issue should be addressed in the next update.
The Qt 5 font weight mismatch should be addressed in a follow-up once the full font-application path is wired through the ThemeManager. Tracked in #21280.

> Qt \<= 6.8 as well as Linux is now treated specially with the palettes as Qt messed up the Theme Palette for those versions

Does "Linux" mean "neither Windows nor macOS", or does it mean "Linux needs to be treated differently from *BSD or Solaris or AIX or other UN\*Xes using an X11-based or Wayland-based window system"?

In this case it means, that the default themes that Qt uses on Linux are mostly only light-mode based and not capable of switching between modes. There are major improvements lately but in general switching through Qt is not possible. I assume the same goes for any other non-Windows and macOS system (just guessing, have not tried). On Windows a similar issue existed until Qt 6.8. macOS on the other hand works fine. 

This is the reason why this includes its own baseline palette for light and dark on Linux and Windows with Qt < 6.8

The problem is a little bit more Qt specific than just that. The baseline issue is the default style selected by Qt (https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtquickcontrols-styles.html#default-styles). For Windows it is a specific Windows style and for Linux or other *NIX based platforms it is the Fusion style (if the package maintainer for that platform did not select a different one). Both do not support Light/Dark out-of-the-box but only a light setting. Some Qt styles are Light/Dark agnostic (like the one chosen for macOS) and some are not. The newest Qt version and the newest styles support Light/Dark. The default style selected for Linux or Windows does not.

The way around this is to catch the proper signals and bring a dark style ourselves. The one we use here, is a style that is actually adopted by the community as a sort-of "Dark Fusion" style (https://gist.github.com/QuantumCD/6245215). With that it becomes a matter of detecting the switch. 

On Windows that has been tricky (prior the latest builds of Win11) as it was not a style change but a ColorScheme Change, but not in any situation .... But at least the detection is pretty stable now for Windows. 

On Linux (and yes, in this case I meant it as a synonym for any form of *NIX) it is way more complicated. Besides the fact that even the FreeDesktop people decided on specific settings to be communicated when choosing light or dark modes, the DM people did not coordinate. So on Gnome, you actually get "default" when light mode is selected (but only when the theme is actually light) and "prefer-dark" when dark mode is selected. You do NOT get "prefer-light", leading to the selection issues mentioned by John. KDE does it right, they send "prefer-dark" and "prefer-light". So far I've only tested those two, Cinnamon is on the Todo list.

Some more comments:
With the light theme, the new color in the Packet List for the selected packet is too close to the default color filter color for UDP packets. It also now responds to the packet list not having focus, changing to a grey color (I'm neutral on this.) Also, previously when hovering the selected packet, the hover color was displayed. This is still true on the Packet Tree, but on the Packet List now the selected color wins when something is both selected and hovered.

When I switch my entire desktop to dark mode on a recent Fedora Linux GNOME desktop, it changes the theme to dark if it's in system default (good). Changing the system to light mode does not change the Wireshark theme back to light, though. It does change it from dark to light once if I initially started Wireshark in both System Default and dark, but only once; repeated switching only works in the light->dark direction.

So at least part of this is because the desktop seems to use `default` for Light mode, and `prefer-dark` for Dark mode, so the former goes into the unknown path. (This seems to be an intentional design choice, at least for now: https://gitlab.gnome.org/Teams/Design/settings-mockups/-/work_items/27 vs https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gnome-control-center/-/work_items/1948 )

Seems to be a problem with the `qApp->styleHints()->colorScheme()` reporting an old value...

So when the GNOME desktop turns to dark, the detector works (it gets `prefer-dark`.) When it goes to `default`, that falls to the Qt path, and `qApp->styleHints()->colorScheme()` seems to generally report the wrong thing (even opposite?) for some reason. Perhaps https://qt-project.atlassian.net/browse/QTBUG-144863

```qApp->styleHints()->colorScheme()``` does not work properly on any Linux platform in any Qt version and on Windows prior to and including Qt 6.8. It should according to the documentation but in reality I went and implemented my own system detector. 

The reason why it is not really working is - at least in my guess - the underlying Qt style. On Linux that is Fusion, and as of 6.11 Fusion does not include a dark mode. Same for the default style on Windows. Later versions of Qt on Windows switched to the Universal style which has a dark mode. The style hints are still not 100% reliable. 

As for why Gnome is doing what Gnome is doing, there is nothing intentional in that design choice, just Gnome being Gnome and making life for developers unnecessarily complicated by design. KDE does it better and sets "prefer-dark" and "prefer-light". Their themes also properly report if they are light or dark versions (at least according to the specs I've looked at). 

Historically the reason for the mess is, that the mode switch was done by selecting a different theme and be done with it. The original implementations did not intend on things like switching the mode depending on the surrounding light intensity or similar ideas. With automatic switching the issue became apparent. Windows had a similar issue, in where they had the signal for the mode change but still omitted only a colorscheme change that could mean dark but could also mean any other color style they supported, therefore not reliably allowing detection. The only system that does it out of the box properly is Mac.

Implementing the themes, I've learned there is something called WCGA factor (https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/). Those define certain arithmetics for good contrasts and visibility. Long story short, they actually define a distance between color values that systems should adhere to be good readable and we did not even got close in the past to be good with ours. That is why some colors look a little bit darker than they used to. But I am still optimising the theme colors (see !25161 for instance). The issue was, that with the big patch I really had a hard time keeping it current with master which is why I merged. I will gradually improve the colors but those are fixes that have no problems happening in a 4.7 branch. @geraldcombs will create the 4.7 branch next Wednesday, hence my hurry getting this in. +# AddTheme.cmake — Handles capsulating themes into Qt resource files
+# This module provides a simple interface for adding themes to the Qt resource file.
+# It requires QrcBuilder.cmake to be included before it.
+#
+# add_theme(<disk_name> [<alias>])
+# 	Adds a theme to the list of themes to be included in the Qt resource file.
+# 	The disk_name is the name of the theme directory under resources/themes,
+# 	and alias is an optional name to use in the resource file instead of the disk name.
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+
+if(NOT COMMAND qrc_add_file)
+    message(FATAL_ERROR
+        "AddThemes.cmake requires QrcBuilder.cmake to be included first. "
+        "Add 'include(QrcBuilder)' before 'include(AddThemes)'.")
+endif()
+
+function(add_theme)
+    cmake_parse_arguments(ARG "" "NAME;ALIAS;TARGET" "" ${ARGN})
+    if(NOT ARG_NAME)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "add_theme: NAME is required")
+    endif()
+
+    set(_theme_name "${ARG_NAME}")
+    set(_alias_name "${ARG_NAME}")
+    if(ARG_ALIAS)
+        set(_alias_name "${ARG_ALIAS}")
+    endif()
+
+    qrc_add_file(NAME themes
+                 FILE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/themes/${_theme_name}/theme.jsonc"
+                 ALIAS "${_alias_name}/theme.jsonc"
+		 TARGET "${ARG_TARGET}")
+
+endfunction()

+// =====================================================================
+// Wireshark Default Theme
+// =====================================================================
+//
+// The built-in theme shipped with Wireshark.  Every value here serves
+// as the fallback for custom themes — custom themes only need to
+// override what they want to change.
+//
+// Format: JSONC — standard JSON with C-style comments.
+//
+// Color value convention:
+//   Each color is { "light": "#hex", "dark": "#hex" }.
+//   "light" is used when the system/user selects light appearance,
+//   "dark" when dark appearance is active.
+//
+// Color formats accepted:
+//   "#rrggbb"              — opaque hex
+//   "#rrggbbaa"            — hex with alpha
+//   "rgba(r, g, b, a)"    — CSS-style, alpha 0–255 (QSS convention)
+//
+// To create a custom theme, copy this file, change "name", and adjust
+// any values you like.  Place it in your personal configuration
+// directory under themes/<name>/theme.jsonc and select it in
+// Edit → Preferences → Appearance.
+// =====================================================================
+
+{
+	// =================================================================
+	// REQUIRED SECTIONS
+	// =================================================================
+
+	"meta": {
+		"name": "Wireshark Default",
+		"version": 1,
+		"author": "Wireshark Foundation",
+		"description": "The built-in Wireshark theme, based on the Tango palette."
+	},
+
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	// Brand — the two colors that define the visual identity.
+	//
+	// "primary" is the main brand hue — drives header gradient end,
+	// selection highlight, section header hover, sparkline stroke,
+	// link accents, and the splash progress bar.
+	//
+	// "deep" is the darkest brand shade — drives header gradient start.
+	//
+	// For dark mode: "primary" is brighter for visibility on dark
+	// surfaces; "deep" is near-black with a hint of the brand hue.
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	"brand": {
+		"primary": { "light": "#2c6fb5", "dark": "#5b9ee6" },
+		"deep":    { "light": "#1e3a5f", "dark": "#0f1b30" }
+	},
+
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	// Accent — four semantic colors.  Required.
+	//
+	// These drive the update bar, filter validation, status indicators,
+	// expert info fallbacks, and the "Development Build" badge.
+	//
+	// Default sources:
+	//   success — Material Design green
+	//   warning — Wireshark orange
+	//   error   — Tango scarlet_4 (light) / scarlet_3 (dark)
+	//   info    — Tango sky_blue_4 (light) / sky_blue_3 (dark)
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	"accent": {
+		"success": { "light": "#4caf50", "dark": "#4caf50" },
+		"warning": { "light": "#e8652d", "dark": "#e8652d" },
+		"error":   { "light": "#cc0000", "dark": "#ef2929" },
+		"info":    { "light": "#3465a4", "dark": "#729fcf" }
+	},
+
+	// =================================================================
+	// OPTIONAL SECTIONS
+	// All of these fall back to derivation from brand/accent when
+	// omitted.  The default theme includes them for documentation
+	// and to serve as the explicit fallback values.
+	// =================================================================
+
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	// Expert info severity colors
+	//
+	// Background colors for expert info items in the protocol tree,
+	// expert info dialog, and analysis views.
+	//
+	// When this section is omitted from a custom theme, colors are
+	// derived from accent values at 40% alpha.
+	//
+	// Origin: inherited from the GTK+ era.  Dark variants are the
+	// same as light — a future iteration should provide proper
+	// dark-mode values.
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	"expert": {
+		"comment":    { "light": "#b7f774", "dark": "#b7f774" },
+		"chat":       { "light": "#80b7f7", "dark": "#80b7f7" },
+		"note":       { "light": "#a0ffff", "dark": "#a0ffff" },
+		"warn":       { "light": "#f7f253", "dark": "#f7f253" },
+		"error":      { "light": "#ff5c5c", "dark": "#ff5c5c" },
+		"foreground": { "light": "#000000", "dark": "#000000" }
+	},
+
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	// Packet display state colors
+	//
+	// For each state the unsuffixed key is the row BACKGROUND tint and
+	// the matching <state>Text key is the FOREGROUND.  Hidden is the
+	// exception — it's text-only (no bg) because it dims items that
+	// render on the normal row background.
+	//
+	// When a *Text key is omitted, ThemeManager derives a foreground
+	// from the bg via contrastingTextColor() (WCAG luminance pick).
+	// When `ignored` (bg) is omitted, the row's normal background is
+	// used unchanged.
+	//
+	// Light defaults: selection is a saturated brand blue so it stays
+	// distinct from the pale pastel color-filter rule backgrounds
+	// (active=#FFFFFF on #2C6FB5, marked=#FFFFFF on #002033, …).

+	//
+	// Derivation when the section is omitted entirely:

+	//   marked         = darken(brand.primary, 65%)
+	//   markedText     = contrastingText(marked)
+	//   ignored        = (none) → row default bg
+	//   ignoredText    = text @ 50% alpha
+	//   hidden         = text @ 40% alpha
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	"packets": {
+		"selection":     { "light": "#2c6fb5", "dark": "#2a3a55" },
+		"selectionText": { "light": "#ffffff", "dark": "#e8e8e8" },
+		"inactive":      { "light": "#efefef", "dark": "#2a2c42" },

+		"marked":        { "light": "#002033", "dark": "#002033" },
+		"markedText":    { "light": "#ffffff", "dark": "#ffffff" },

+	},

+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	"conversation": {
+		"client":     { "light": "#fbedcd", "dark": "#3a2010" },
+		"clientText": { "light": "#800000", "dark": "#ffb088" },
+		"server":     { "light": "#edeefb", "dark": "#1a1a3a" },
+		"serverText": { "light": "#000080", "dark": "#a0b4ff" }
+	},
+
+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------
+	// Fonts
+	//
+	// Two base font classes.  All other font usage in the application
+	// is a derivation (different size or weight) from one of these.
+	//
+	// Both "family" and "size" are optional within each class.
+	// When "family" is omitted:
+	//   regular   — system UI font (platform-dependent)
+	//   monospace — platform fallback chain:

+	// -----------------------------------------------------------------

+		// "monospace": { "family": "...", "size": 13 }
+	},

+	//

+	// surface colors (e.g., Solarized, high-contrast).
+	//
+	// 7 supported roles — the only ones Wireshark uses from the

+	//
+	// NOT in this section (auto-derived from brand.primary):

+	//
+	// The default theme intentionally leaves this empty — it uses

+// Wireshark Inverted Theme — Testing Only
+// =====================================================================
+//
+// A deliberately inverted/contrasting theme for testing purposes.
+// Every color is chosen to be visually distinct from the default theme,

+# Wireshark Themes
+
+This directory contains color themes for Wireshark and Stratoshark.  Each
+theme lives in its own subdirectory and is loaded by the `ThemeManager`
+singleton at application startup.
+
+## Directory layout
+
+```
+resources/themes/
+    README.md               ← this file
+    theme.schema.json       ← JSON Schema for theme.jsonc validation
+    default/                ← built-in theme, always present
+        theme.jsonc         ← color definitions (required)
+        images/             ← theme-specific images (optional, future)
+    my-custom-theme/
+        theme.jsonc
+        images/
+            logo.png
+```
+
+Each theme directory **must** contain a `theme.jsonc` file.  It **may**
+contain an `images/` subdirectory for theme-specific assets such as
+background images or logos.
+
+## File format: JSONC
+
+Theme files use **JSONC** — standard JSON with C-style comments (`//`
+line comments and `/* */` block comments).  The ThemeManager strips
+comments before parsing with `QJsonDocument`, so no additional library
+is needed.
+
+## Theme file structure
+
+```jsonc
+{
+    "meta": {
+        "name": "My Theme",
+        "version": 1,
+        "description": "A short description shown in the preferences dialog.",
+        "author": "Your Name"
+    },
+
+    "colors": {
+        "section-name": {
+            "token-name": { "light": "#rrggbb", "dark": "#rrggbb" }
+        }
+    }
+}
+```
+
+A JSON Schema is provided at `theme.schema.json` for validation.
+Editors that support JSON Schema (VS Code, IntelliJ, etc.) can use it
+for autocompletion and error checking by adding a `$schema` reference
+or configuring the schema association in editor settings.
+
+### Top-level fields
+
+| Field   | Type   | Required | Description |
+|---------|--------|----------|-------------|
+| `meta`  | object | yes      | Theme metadata (see below) |
+| `colors`| object | yes      | Nested color definitions |
+
+### `meta` — Theme metadata
+
+| Field         | Type   | Required | Description |
+|---------------|--------|----------|-------------|
+| `name`        | string | yes      | Display name shown in preferences |
+| `version`     | int    | yes      | Schema version, currently `1` |
+| `description` | string | no       | One-line description |
+| `author`      | string | no       | Theme author or organization |
+
+### Color values
+
+Each color token is an object with `"light"` and `"dark"` keys.
+Accepted formats:
+
+| Format                  | Example                    | Notes |
+|-------------------------|----------------------------|-------|
+| `#rrggbb`               | `"#2c6fb5"`                | Opaque hex |
+| `#rrggbbaa`             | `"#2c6fb580"`              | Hex with alpha |
+| `rgba(r, g, b, a)`      | `"rgba(76,175,80,51)"`     | CSS-style, alpha 0-255 (QSS convention) |
+
+### Token naming in QSS
+
+Nested keys are joined with dots to form the QSS token name, prefixed
+and suffixed with `@`:
+
+```jsonc
+// In theme.jsonc:
+"header": {
+    "gradient-start": { "light": "#1e3a5f", "dark": "#0f1b30" }
+}
+```
+
+```css
+/* In a .qss file: */
+#welcomeHeader {
+    background: qlineargradient(
+        stop:0 @header.gradient-start@,
+        stop:1 @header.gradient-end@
+    );
+}
+```
+
+The ThemeManager resolves `@header.gradient-start@` to `#1e3a5f` (light)
+or `#0f1b30` (dark) depending on the current appearance.
+
+## Color sections reference
+
+The default theme defines the following sections.  Custom themes should
+provide values for all tokens to ensure complete coverage; any missing
+token falls back to the default theme's value.
+
+### `text` — Global text colors
+
+| Token            | Purpose |
+|------------------|---------|
+| `primary`        | Primary content text |
+| `muted`          | Secondary labels, file sizes, metadata |
+| `on-dark`        | Text on dark gradient backgrounds (always white) |
+| `on-dark-muted`  | De-emphasized text on dark backgrounds (50% white) |
+
+### `accent` — Global accent colors
+
+| Token    | Purpose |
+|----------|---------|
+| `blue`   | Wireshark brand blue, links, interactive highlights |
+| `green`  | Success/update contexts, pulsing dot, download button |
+| `orange` | Development badge, warning accent |
+
+### `content` — Content area backgrounds
+
+| Token           | Purpose |
+|-----------------|---------|
+| `bg`            | Main content area background |
+| `border`        | Dividers, card borders, separators |
+| `hover-bg`      | Row hover in file lists, interface lists |
+| `selected-bg`   | Selected row background |
+| `selected-text`  | Selected row text |
+| `sidebar-bg`    | Learn card and sidebar backgrounds |
+
+### `header` — Welcome page header bar
+
+| Token            | Purpose |
+|------------------|---------|
+| `gradient-start` | Left/top stop of the blue gradient |
+| `gradient-end`   | Right/bottom stop of the blue gradient |
+
+### `update` — Update notification bar
+
+| Token                | Purpose |
+|----------------------|---------|
+| `gradient-start`     | Left stop of the green gradient |
+| `gradient-end`       | Right stop of the green gradient |
+| `border`             | Bottom border of the update bar |
+| `text`               | Primary update message text |
+| `text-highlight`     | Bold version name within the message |
+| `link`               | "Release Notes" link color |
+| `link-hover`         | Link hover state |
+| `link-pressed`       | Link pressed state |
+| `btn-bg`             | "Download Update" button background |
+| `btn-hover`          | Button hover |
+| `btn-pressed`        | Button pressed |
+| `btn-disabled-bg`    | Button disabled background |
+| `btn-disabled-text`  | Button disabled text |
+| `dismiss-hover-bg`   | Dismiss "x" hover background |
+| `dismiss-pressed-bg` | Dismiss "x" pressed background |
+
+### `section` — Section headers (Open, Capture, Learn)
+
+| Token          | Purpose |
+|----------------|---------|
+| `header`       | Default text color for section titles |
+| `header-hover` | Hover color for clickable section titles |
+
+### `expert` — Expert info severity colors
+
+| Token        | Purpose |
+|--------------|---------|
+| `comment`    | Green — Comment severity |
+| `chat`       | Light blue — Chat severity |
+| `note`       | Bright turquoise — Note severity |
+| `warn`       | Yellow — Warning severity |
+| `error`      | Pale red — Error severity |
+| `foreground` | Text color on expert info backgrounds |
+
+These colors originated in the GTK+ era and currently have no
+dark-specific variants.  The `foreground` value (`#000000`) will need
+adjustment for dark mode in a future iteration.
+
+### `proto` — Protocol tree
+
+| Token    | Purpose |
+|----------|---------|
+| `hidden` | Color for hidden protocol items when display is enabled |
+
+### `status` — Status bar and warnings
+
+| Token        | Purpose |
+|--------------|---------|
+| `warning-bg` | Warning background (status bar, time shift dialog) |
+
+### `json` — JSON syntax highlighting
+
+| Token       | Purpose |
+|-------------|---------|
+| `key`       | JSON object keys |
+| `string`    | String values |
+| `primitive` | Numbers, booleans, null |
+
+### `graph` — Graph colors (1-14)
+
+Rotating color cycle for I/O graphs, TCP stream graphs, LTE RLC
+graphs, and RTP player scatter plots.  Slots 1-7 are saturated,
+8-14 are pastel.  All derived from the Tango palette.
+
+### `sequence` — Sequence diagram colors (1-10)
+
+Rotating pastel backgrounds for flow/sequence diagrams.  Inherited
+from GTK+ `graph_analysis.c`.  Currently identical in light and dark.
+
+## Creating a custom theme
+
+1. Copy the `default/` directory to a new directory name:
+   ```
+   cp -r resources/themes/default resources/themes/my-theme
+   ```
+
+2. Edit `my-theme/theme.jsonc`:
+   - Change `"name"` to your theme's display name
+   - Adjust any colors you want to customize
+   - Add images to `my-theme/images/` if desired
+
+3. Missing tokens fall back to the default theme, so you only need to
+   override the colors you want to change.
+
+4. Place the directory in your personal configuration directory under
+   `themes/` and select it in Edit -> Preferences -> Appearance.
+
+## Relationship to Qt palette
+
+The theme file defines colors for Wireshark-specific UI elements.  The
+standard Qt palette roles (`base`, `text`, `window`, `highlight`, etc.)
+remain OS-provided by default.  Stylesheet files may still use
+`palette(base)`, `palette(text)`, etc. for structural colors that should
+follow the platform convention.
+
+A future extension may allow themes to override palette roles via an
+optional `"palette"` section, enabling full visual control without
+modifying system settings.

+#
+# Wireshark tests
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+#
+'''Theme system tests.
+
+Validates that every bundled `theme.jsonc` under `resources/themes/*/`
+loads cleanly against `resources/themes/theme.schema.json`.
+
+Purpose: catch drift between `ThemeParser` and the schema.  If a
+contributor adds a new section or key to the parser but forgets the
+schema, the next bundled theme to use that key (or any negative test
+that relies on `additionalProperties: false`) will fail this test.
+
+`jsonschema` is an optional test dependency; tests self-skip when the
+package is not installed so existing `pip install pytest pytest-xdist`
+setups keep working.
+'''
+
+import json
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+SCHEMA_PATH = REPO_ROOT / 'resources' / 'themes' / 'theme.schema.json'
+THEME_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / 'resources' / 'themes'
+
+
+def _strip_jsonc(text):
+    '''Strip // line comments, /* block */ comments, and trailing commas.
+
+    Mirrors `ThemeParser::stripComments` in
+    `ui/qt/utils/themes/theme_parser.cpp` (preserves strings, preserves
+    newlines so JSON parse-error line numbers stay meaningful).
+    '''
+    out = []
+    i = 0
+    n = len(text)
+    while i < n:
+        c = text[i]
+        if c == '"':
+            out.append(c)
+            i += 1
+            while i < n:
+                d = text[i]
+                out.append(d)
+                i += 1
+                if d == '\\' and i < n:
+                    out.append(text[i])
+                    i += 1
+                elif d == '"':
+                    break
+            continue
+        if c == '/' and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '/':
+            i += 2
+            while i < n and text[i] != '\n':
+                i += 1
+            continue
+        if c == '/' and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '*':
+            i += 2
+            while i + 1 < n and not (text[i] == '*' and text[i + 1] == '/'):
+                if text[i] == '\n':
+                    out.append('\n')
+                i += 1
+            i += 2
+            continue
+        out.append(c)
+        i += 1
+    stripped = ''.join(out)
+    # JSONC tolerates trailing commas; strict JSON does not.
+    return re.sub(r',(\s*[}\]])', r'\1', stripped)
+
+
+def _bundled_themes():
+    return sorted(THEME_ROOT.glob('*/theme.jsonc'))
+
+
+class TestThemeSchema:
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize('theme_path', _bundled_themes(),
+                             ids=lambda p: p.parent.name)
+    def test_bundled_theme_matches_schema(self, theme_path):
+        '''Every bundled theme.jsonc validates against theme.schema.json.'''
+        jsonschema = pytest.importorskip('jsonschema')
+
+        schema = json.loads(SCHEMA_PATH.read_text())
+        data = json.loads(_strip_jsonc(theme_path.read_text()))
+        jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(data)

+/**
+ * Pure color-math helpers, independent of the running app's theme or
+ * palette.
+ *
+ * Every method is static and side-effect-free except
+ * contrastingText(QColor) which — when the surface has alpha — asks
+ * ThemeManager for the current app mode to pick a fallback backdrop.
+ * That coupling is deliberate: the caller wants "the right foreground
+ * for this translucent surface as rendered right now", which is a
+ * theme-runtime question.
+ */
+class ColorMath
+{
+public:
+    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
+    // Luminance & contrast
+    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    /** WCAG relative luminance in the [0, 1] range. */
+    static double relativeLuminance(const QColor &color);
+
+    /** WCAG contrast ratio between two opaque colors.  Higher values
+     *  are more contrasty; 4.5 is the AA threshold for body text. */
+    static qreal constrastRatio(const QColor &color1, const QColor &color2);
+
+    /** Returns true if the given color's relative luminance is below
+     *  the WCAG equal-contrast threshold (≈0.179).  Purely a color-
+     *  math helper; independent of the running app's theme. */
+    static bool isDark(const QColor &color);
+
+    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
+    // Mix / shade
+    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    /** Linear blend of two colors at ratio `r`.  r=0 returns a, r=1
+     *  returns b.  Alpha-aware. */
+    static QColor         mix(const QColor &a, const QColor &b, qreal ratio = 0.5);
+    static ThemeColorPair mix(const ThemeColorPair &a, const ThemeColorPair &b, qreal ratio = 0.5);
+
+    /** Mix the given color with black at percent %.  Hover typically
+     *  8-12 %, pressed 16-20 %, gradient backdrop 50-65 %. */
+    static QColor         darken(const QColor &c, int percent);
+    static ThemeColorPair darken(const ThemeColorPair &p, int percent);
+
+    /** Mix the given color with white at percent %.  Used for text on
+     *  dark surfaces (30-70 %). */
+    static QColor         lighten(const QColor &c, int percent);

+    // ---------------------------------------------------------------

+/**

+ *
+ * Owned and operated exclusively by ThemeManager.  No other component
+ * in Wireshark should construct, query, or connect to a detector
+ * instance; everything outside the theme subsystem asks
+ * ThemeManager::isDark() instead.
+ *
+ * The detector begins observing the system setting in its constructor
+ * and tears the observer down in its destructor (RAII).  There is
+ * deliberately no start()/stop() pair.
+ *
+ * The actual observation mechanism is platform-specific.  A concrete
+ * Impl is provided per platform in
+ *   ui/qt/utils/themes/system_theme_detector_mac.mm    (macOS)
+ *   ui/qt/utils/themes/system_theme_detector_win.cpp   (Windows)
+ *   ui/qt/utils/themes/system_theme_detector_unix.cpp  (Linux/BSD)
+ *   ui/qt/utils/themes/system_theme_detector_stub.cpp  (all other builds)
+ *
+ * CMake selects exactly one of those for the build.
+ */

+        Unknown,    ///< The platform could not determine a preference (stub

+ * map and mode, and pushes it via `QApplication::setPalette()`.

+ *   - macOS (any supported Qt) and Windows on Qt ≥ 6.8: a caller-

+ *     pristine) and refreshes it whenever the effective scheme flips.

+ *     builder has pushed any palette via `setPalette()`, subsequent
+ *     reads return that customized palette — so consecutive theme
+ *     switches would accumulate overrides instead of restarting from a
+ *     clean OS baseline.

+ *     light or dark palette** (see `builtInLightPalette()` /
+ *     `builtInDarkPalette()`).  The Linux platform themes
+ *     (gnome/gtk3/qt6ct) silently ignore `QStyleHints::setColorScheme()`
+ *     and pin both the hint and `standardPalette()` to the OS value,
+ *     which makes "Dark mode on a Light OS" (or vice versa)
+ *     impossible to honor without supplying our own palette.  Old
+ *     Fusion has the same problem.  `osBaseline` is ignored on these
+ *     platforms.
+ *

+ * `theme.jsonc`) are applied on top of the baseline.  Brand-driven
+ * roles (`Highlight`, `Link`, `Accent`, `HighlightedText`) are always
+ * overlaid last, so themes don't need to set them.
+ */

+{
+public:
+    using TokenMap = QHash<ThemeManager::ThemeToken, ThemeColorPair>;
+
+    /**
+     * Build and return the full QPalette from the token map without
+     * pushing it to QApplication.  Callers that need the palette value
+     * before it is applied (e.g. to derive tokens first) should call
+     * this and then push the result themselves via
+     * `QApplication::setPalette()`.
+     *

+     *                          accent, optional palette overrides).
+     * @param isDarkMode        Which side of color pairs to use.
+     * @param tokenNameCache    Map "palettewindow" → ThemeToken::PaletteWindow

+     *                          lowercased enumerator name.

+     *                          ThemeManager; used as the baseline on
+     *                          macOS and Windows Qt ≥ 6.8.  Ignored on
+     *                          Linux and Windows Qt < 6.8.

+                          bool                                                isDarkMode,

+/**
+ * Loads a QSS stylesheet from the built-in `:/stylesheets/` resource
+ * tree and resolves every `wstheme(RoleName)` token by looking up
+ * RoleName in the current theme's color map.
+ *
+ * Split out of ThemeManager so the loader logic — stylesheet path
+ * sanitization, QSS read, token regex, role-enum lookup — lives
+ * alongside the other theme helpers under `ui/qt/utils/themes/`.
+ *
+ * Stateless: every call reads fresh resource contents and resolves
+ * tokens against the token map the caller provides.  ThemeManager is
+ * the usual caller and passes its own `themeColors_` / `isDarkMode()`.
+ */
+class ThemeStyleSheetLoader
+{
+public:
+    using TokenMap = QHash<ThemeManager::ThemeToken, ThemeColorPair>;
+
+    /**
+     * Load `:/stylesheets/<name>.qss` and return its contents with:
+     *
+     *   - every `wstheme(RoleName)` token replaced by the resolved
+     *     `#rrggbb` hex of the corresponding ThemeToken, picked from
+     *     `tokens` using `isDarkMode` to choose the light/dark side;
+     *   - every literal `%wsmode%` occurrence replaced by the string
+     *     `"dark"` or `"light"` — intended for picking mode-specific
+     *     asset filenames inside `image: url(...)` rules, e.g.
+     *       image: url(:/stock_icons/14x14/x-filter-dropdown.%wsmode%.png);
+     *     The `%wsmode%` placeholder takes no arguments and is a plain
+     *     text substitution; it runs before the `wstheme(...)`
+     *     regex pass.
+     *
+     * Returns an empty QString on any of:
+     *   - `name` is empty or contains illegal characters / path
+     *     traversal attempts (`..`, leading `/`, leading `.`,
+     *     backslash, etc.)
+     *   - The resource file cannot be opened.
+     *
+     * Tokens that don't resolve (unknown role name or missing color
+     * in the map) are **stripped** from the output and a `qWarning`
+     * is emitted — Qt's QSS parser is all-or-nothing per object, so
+     * leaving a literal `wstheme(Foo)` in place would silently drop
+     * the entire rule on the first typo; stripping keeps the rest
+     * of the rules valid and the warning surfaces the typo.
+     *
+     * @param name       Logical name under :/stylesheets/, without
+     *                   extension (e.g. "widgets/learn-card").
+     * @param tokens     Current theme's color map.
+     * @param isDarkMode Which side of color pairs to select.
+     */
+    static QString load(const QString  &name,
+                        const TokenMap &tokens,
+                        bool            isDarkMode);
+};

+/* ===================================================================
+ * AccordionFrame — sliding collapsible search / navigation toolbar
+ *
+ * Used by "Go to packet", "Find packet", and similar toolbars docked
+ * at the top of the main window.  The frame itself animates via
+ * QPropertyAnimation on maximumHeight from C++; the colours and
+ * border here are purely the static appearance.
+ *
+ * This stylesheet is applied to an AccordionFrame instance via
+ * ThemeManager::styleSheet("widgets/accordion-frame"), so all
+ * selectors target the frame and its descendants.
+ *
+ * Colour sourcing: native `palette(mid)` — Qt resolves against the
+ * current QPalette at render time, so the border automatically
+ * follows light/dark mode via ThemePaletteBuilder's palette output.
+ * No wstheme(...) tokens are needed here; this is a pure-palette
+ * widget.
+ * =================================================================== */
+
+/* Cap the width of the "go to packet" line edit so the field doesn't
+ * stretch across the whole toolbar on wide main windows. */
+QLineEdit#goToLineEdit {
+    max-width: 5em;
+}
+
+/* Subtle rounded border on line-edits inside the frame.  Originally
+ * macOS-only, where QLineEdit rendered without a visible native
+ * border inside our custom QFrame; kept universally for a consistent
+ * look across platforms. */
+QLineEdit {
+    border: 1px solid palette(mid);
+    border-radius: 3px;
+    padding: 1px;
+}

+/* ===================================================================
+ * Wireshark Bluetooth Dialog Tables — Hover Indicator
+ *
+ * Shared stylesheet for the four Bluetooth analysis dialogs that
+ * present a tree- or table-view of host/controller data:
+ *
+ *   BluetoothHciSummaryDialog            (QTreeWidget)
+ *   BluetoothDevicesDialog               (QTreeWidget)
+ *   BluetoothAttServerAttributesDialog   (QTreeWidget)
+ *   BluetoothDeviceDialog                (QTableWidget)
+ *
+ * Each dialog applies this stylesheet to its top-level view via
+ *
+ *   widget->setStyleSheet(ThemeManager::styleSheet(
+ *       QStringLiteral("widgets/bluetooth-table")));
+ *
+ * and re-applies it on ThemeManager::themeChanged.  The selectors
+ * scope to the widget the stylesheet is set on, so listing both
+ * QTreeView::item and QTableView::item here is harmless — only the
+ * matching one fires for any given dialog.
+ *
+ * Colors use palette() (not wstheme()) so the hover tint follows
+ * the Qt palette in both light and dark modes — matching the
+ * subtle hover convention already established by welcome-page.qss
+ * for QAbstractItemView items.
+ * =================================================================== */
+
+QTreeView::item:hover,
+QTableView::item:hover {
+    background-color: palette(midlight);
+    color: palette(text);
+}
